She stated the Prime Minister's forgiveness was a birthday gift and a new lease of life. The mother appealed for the withdrawal of the FIR, claiming her daughter's age was incorrectly stated. She requested stricter social media controls for minors and their exclusion from protests.

title: 'Took my jewellery': Actor Aditi Sharma accuses husband, in-laws of domestic abuse

The actress alleged domestic abuse by her husband and his family members. Police have launched an investigation and are recording statements from all parties. Further action will be taken after evidence collection and examination.

title: Huge blow! Jasprit Bumrah ruled out of Sri Lanka Tests | Exclusive
content: Star bowler Jasprit Bumrah will miss the upcoming Test series against Sri Lanka. He continues to feel discomfort in his left knee after an initial assessment. Stakeholders have decided it is not safe to push him back into cricket. A full recovery is now the primary focus for the Indian team. The two-Test series is scheduled to begin on August 15.

title: 'Buy police uniforms, head to Jantar Mantar': Inside 'Pakistan-linked' terror plot
content: West Bengal Police STF arrested Arpita Sarkar, girlfriend of suspected terrorist Hamim Mondal.  Investigators are probing their alleged plan to create disturbances at Jantar Mantar.  Hamim was reportedly working under instructions from Pakistani handlers via social media.  Arpita is also suspected of involvement in a honey-trap network targeting influential people.  The investigation is ongoing, and more arrests are anticipated in the coming days.

title: Jeff Bezos warns Mamdani on NYC taxes, slams wasteful spending
content: Jeff Bezos commented on New York City's proposed pied-à-terre tax. He suggested that aggressive tax increases could negatively impact tourism and competitiveness. Bezos also criticized targeting individuals, calling it a villain strategy. He argued that government spending inefficiencies are a greater concern than taxation. Bezos previously criticized the city's public school spending and economic policies.

title: 8 dead as heavy rain wreaks havoc, triggers landslides, floods across Kerala
content: Kerala faces severe rain and flooding, resulting in at least eight fatalities. Landslides and inundation have caused widespread damage across several districts. Rescue operations are underway for stranded residents and missing fishermen. Authorities have opened relief camps and issued alerts for continuing rainfall. Tourist destinations remain temporarily closed due to the ongoing adverse weather conditions.

title: RBI deposit rules: Differential rates, daily disclosures changes explained
content: The Reserve Bank of India has revised rules for bulk deposits, effective October 2026. Banks can now offer differential interest rates based on liquidity risk under the LCR framework. This move aligns deposit pricing with revised LCR guidelines for better asset-liability management. Mandatory daily public disclosure of bulk deposit rates will enhance transparency for customers. However, uniform rates will continue for similarly placed depositors across all branches.

title: 150-year-overdue library book returned in Australia; racks up Rs 16 lakh 'late fee'
content: A library received a book returned after 150 years overdue.  The calculated late fee reached approximately twenty-eight thousand Australian dollars.  This rare book was discovered during home renovations and was damaged.  It was borrowed by a local resident's great-great-grandfather in the 1870s.  The book will now join the library's local history collection.

title: When a district in Florida's Everglades used robot rabbits to eliminate Burmese pythons
content: Florida is employing AI-powered robot rabbits to help locate invasive Burmese pythons. These solar-powered decoys mimic prey using heat and scent to lure snakes. When a python is detected, officials are alerted to remove the invasive species. This technology complements the annual Python Challenge, which has removed thousands of snakes. These efforts aim to control the python population impacting native wildlife.

title: Maddy Murphy, 16, travels 15,000km to join Swiss ballet academy
content: Sixteen-year-old Maddy Murphy, who grew up in the remote Queensland town of Julia Creek, is set to travel nearly 15,000 kilometres to Switzerland after earning a place at the prestigious Tanz Akademie Zurich. After years of balancing ballet, distance education and multiple moves for training, she hopes to become a professional company dancer while inspiring other children from rural communities to follow their dreams.

title: 113-million-year-old fossils reveal how volcanic CO2 caused plankton extinction
content: Tiny fossils reveal ocean acidification caused a major planktic foraminifera extinction. Massive volcanic eruptions released carbon dioxide, making ocean waters more acidic. This chemical shift hindered shell formation for these vital marine organisms. Researchers used calcium isotopes in shells to find this missing evidence. The findings offer insights into modern ocean acidification's potential impacts.

title: Nuclear plants, Gaza craters: Google pulls AI tool from Google Earth in 24 hours
content: Google has removed its new AI image generation feature from Google Earth. This action followed immediate concerns raised by researchers about disinformation risks. Experts warned the tool could easily create convincing fake satellite imagery for public deception. Google stated they are implementing stronger safeguards while pausing the feature. The company noted generated images were watermarked as AI-created.

title: Nanaji Deshmukh Awas Yojana: How workers can avail Rs 1.6 lakh housing aid

To qualify, applicants must have been registered with the welfare board for a minimum of two years. Following the acquisition of an e-Nirman Card and house allotment, they can submit their applications. Those approved will receive ₹1.6 lakh to assist in home ownership.

title: Bobby Fischer: The champion America summoned, and Iceland sheltered
content: Henry Kissinger once urged Bobby Fischer to face the Soviets. It was a small island, not his homeland, that gave him a resting place. In the second column of The Grandmaster View, India's 93rd Grandmaster Aarav Dengla traces Fischer's journey from Cold War hero to exiled genius. his revolutionary impact on chess, the tragedy of his later years, and why the country that embraced him in death offered the sense of belonging that his own homeland ultimately could not.
